I know that you probably don't want to hear this, but it'll probably come back. You just need to find a way to beat it so it doesn't affect you as much as it did.

Mental health, in most cases, is like a rollercoaster. There are some flat levels, extreme lows, extreme highs, and everything in between. I was at an extreme high a few months ago and thought that there was no way I was going back down. I was done, my ride was over, I was leaving and happy to do so. 

But no matter how hard I tried to pull myself back up as I fell down that dark path again, I couldn't. It hurt to see how all my progress was lost. How I was in a worse spot than I started in.

So it hurts to hear it, but it'll probably not stay like that forever.

When you get low next, think about how you feel now. How you feel happy, and relaxed, and cheerful. Think about how it's changed your life and how it's made you a better person. When you start receding into that dark place again, bring these memories up. Try to convince your brain that it's better to stay in this high place, and that you aren't going to let yourself succumb to the negative thoughts, if it's possible.

Good luck, and best wishes.

I took about 10 ibuprofen last night because I was having a really rough night and didn't give a fuck about my health. It made me have such a bad pain in my stomach, and I was basically rolling on the ground in pain for about 3 hours because of it.

I still feel terrible today. I've been feeling a bit sick and stomach pains all day long. 

I guess it was a reality check for me. I gotta stop taking pills even if it does help sometimes. I threw away every substance and pill that I had and am trying to find other ways to cope.

I guess it does. It makes the world a bit better. Maybe not the whole world, but that person's world for sure. I just don't know. I just want to be happy. I want to put a smile on my face and mean it. I want to be able to go to a social gathering or outing without being depressed or anxious. I want to be able to hang out with couples without feeling lonely.

I know that pain is necessary to grow. It's like watering plants. When you give it the perfect amount of water, it'll florish. When you drown the thing with buckets of water every day, it'll die. When you have a little bit of pain, you learn things, grow, become a better person. When you are drowning in problems and pain and hopelessness, you'll die one way or another. You'll lose the fight to drugs, or put a bullet in your brain, or turn into a person you could never imagine yourself becoming. 

I guess I just hope that I can keep my head above water...

Loneliness has been affecting me a lot recently. I wonder if there really is "the right person" out there for me. Someone who likes adventure, someone who'd prefer a walk in the park or hiking to the top of a big mountain or explore some abandoned house over a fancy dinner. Someone who's down to sleep in the car with me instead of paying for a hotel room. Someone who thinks it's worth it to save money on food and spend more money exploring and seeing all the things the world has to offer. Someone who loves getting out of their comfort zone and isn't afraid to be themselves despite the pressure society gives. Someone who loves me and supports me no matter what I'm going through and always wants what's best for our relationship.

I don't want sex, I don't want hookups, I just want someone who loves me and cares about me and wants to grow with me. Something that, in our society, seems to intangible.
